sources.summary: The mobility paradigm focuses on the study, design, and planning of human movement rather than on vehicles. This shift from the object—the car—to the subject—the person—requires a more complex perspective, one that is both granular and comprehensive, as its analytical scope transcends the concrete event of travel and incorporates the subjective and latent aspects that turn displacement into a social practice.
